title: Mosaic: Harnessing the Micro-Architectural Resources of Servers in Serverless Environments
problem: Modern server-class processors suffer from inefficient utilization in serverless environments due to frequent context switches within function invocations and high core oversubscription, causing functions to lose micro-architectural state in caches, TLBs, and branch predictors.
motivation: Serverless computing requires efficient resource utilization to optimize cloud provider infrastructure for the increasingly popular lightweight function execution model.
method: Mosaic introduces MosaicCPU, which partitions micro-architectural structures (caches, TLBs, branch predictors) into tiles assigned to functions, retaining their state across context switches and placing inactive tiles in low-power modes. MosaicScheduler maximizes efficiency through predictive right-sizing of per-function tiles and smart scheduling based on tile state.
key_novelty: Tiling micro-architectural resources on a per-function basis to preserve architectural state across context switches, eliminating performance degradation from repeated cache and predictor misses in serverless workloads.
contributions: MosaicCPU processor architecture with partitioned micro-architectural tiles for serverless workloads
MosaicScheduler software stack with predictive right-sizing and state-aware function scheduling
225% throughput improvement with 22% power reduction compared to conventional server-class processors
Maintains support for traditional monolithic applications alongside serverless workloads
